instruction: Find all files with extension ".ipynb" (excluding those containing "failed" in the name) in the test_environment directory tree and copy them to a new directory "./successful" while preserving directory structure

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 'alt', 't'); time.sleep(0.5)
import pyautogui; import time; time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.write('cd test_environment'); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.press('enter')

result.command: cd /home/user/test_environment && find successful -type f -name '*.ipynb' 2>/dev/null | sort || echo ''

metadata.explanation: Task requires copying .ipynb files that do NOT contain 'failed' in the name. Based on setup.sh, there are 5 .ipynb files total: a_failed.ipynb, b.ipynb, c_failed.ipynb, d.ipynb, e_failed.ipynb. The non-failed ones are: dir1/b.ipynb and dir2/d.ipynb. These should be copied to successful/ with directory structure preserved. Uses existing check_include_exclude metric.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter logic correctly extracts the list of copied .ipynb files from the successful/ directory using find command

Metric check_include_exclude properly verifies both requirements: (1) presence of all expected files (successful/dir1/b.ipynb, successful/dir2/d.ipynb), and (2) absence of any files containing 'failed' in the result
Expected values are semantically correct based on the setup.sh context - correctly identifies the 2 non-failed .ipynb files out of 5 total files
Directory structure preservation is implicitly verified by the full paths in the include list
Complete coverage: evaluator checks all instruction requirements (file type, exclusion pattern, destination directory, structure preservation)
